question: The company matches 6% of my 401(k). Should I also open a Roth IRA, and which comes first?

fields.name: retirement.match_tiers
fields.source_text: Tyler will match 50% of the first 6% of your eligible contributions.

figures.label: Most the match is worth, as % of pay
Step 1: 401(k) at 6% for the full match
Step 3: Roth IRA ($7,500 limit), per check
Step 4: extra 401(k) with what is left
Step 2 if on the HDHP: your own HSA money to the limit, per check

must_include: Corrects the premise: Tyler matches 50% of the first 6%, worth 3% of pay; contribute 6% to get all of it.
Step 1: 401(k) at 6%, about $196.15 per check, for about $98.08 per check ($2,550 a year) of match.
Step 2: HSA only on the HDHP (about $140.38 per check to the limit after Tyler's $750); skipped on the PPO 750.
Step 3: Roth IRA, about $288.46 per check.
Step 4: about $115.39 per check left for extra 401(k) on a $600 goal.
Tyler's match vests 20% a year over the first five years.
Cites page 5 of the Tyler summary for the match.
must_not_include: Roth IRA before the full 401(k) match.
Saying the match is 6% of pay.

assumptions: Profile 'tyler': $85,000 rounded salary, PPO 750, $600 savings goal per check, 3-month emergency fund.
Same order of operations as ex3-match-then-roth.
